cues.text: Good morning. Stretton Festival box office. How can I help you?
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Oh, hello. My family and I are on holiday on the area, and we’ve seen some posters about the festival this week. Could you tell me about some of the events, please?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Of course.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: First of all, are there still tickets available for the jazz band on Saturday?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: There are, but only £15. The £12 seats have all been sold.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: OK. And the venue is the school, isn’t it?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Yes, that’s right, the secondary school. Make sure you don’t go to the primary school by mistake! And there’s an additional performer who isn’t mentioned on the posters – Carolyn Hart is going to play with the band.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Oh, I think I’ve heard her on the radio. Doesn’t she play the oboe, or flute or something?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Yes the flute. She usually plays with symphony orchestras, and apparently this is her first time with a jazz band.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Well, I’d certainly like to hear her. Then the next thing I want to ask about is the duck races – I saw a poster beside a river. What are they, exactly?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Well, you buy a yellow plastic duck – or as many as you like – they’re a pound each. And you write your name on each one. There’ll be several races, depending on the number of ducks taking part. And John Stevens, a champion swimmer who lives locally, is going to start the races. All the ducks will be launched into the river at the back of the cinema, then they’ll float along the river for 500 metres, as far as the railway bridge.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: And are there any prizes?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Yes, the first duck in each race to arrive at the finishing line wins its owner free tickets for the concert on the last night of the festival.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: You said you can buy a duck? I’m sure my children will both want one.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: They’re on sale at a stall in the market. You can’t miss it – it’s got an enormous sign showing a couple of ducks.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: OK. I’ll go there this afternoon. I remember walking past there yesterday. Now could you tell me something about the flower show, please?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Well, admission is free, and the show is being held in Bythwaite Hall.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Sorry, how do you spell that?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: B-Y-T-H-W-A-I-T-E. Bythwaite.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Is it easy to find? I’m not very familiar with the town yet.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Oh, you won’t have any problem. It’s right in the centre of Stretton. It’s the only old building in the town, so it’s easy to recognise.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: I know it. I presume it’s open all day.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Yes, but if you’d like to see the prizes being awarded for the best flowers, you’ll need to be there at 5 o’clock. The prizes are being given by a famous actor, Kevin Shapless. He lives nearby and gets involved in a lot of community events.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Gosh, I’ve seen him on TV. I’ll definitely go to the prize-giving.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: I’ve seen a list of plays that are being performed this week, and I’d like to know which are suitable for my children, and which ones my husband and I might go to.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: How old are your children?
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Five and seven. What about ‘The Mystery of Muldoon’?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: That’s aimed at five to ten-year-olds.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: So if I take my children, I can expect them to enjoy it more than I do?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: I think so. If you’d like something for yourself and your husband and leave your children with a babysitter, you might like to see ‘Fire and Flood’ – it’s about events that really happened in Stretton two hundred years ago, and children might find it rather frightening.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: Oh, thanks for the warning. And finally, what about ‘Silly Sailor’?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: That’s a comedy, and it’s for young and old. In fact, it won an award in the Stretton Drama Festival a couple of months ago.
cues.speaker: ROB

cues.text: OK. Well, goodbye, and thanks for all the information. I’m looking forward to the festival!
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Goodbye.
cues.speaker: ROB
